sections.h2: Which court handles an eviction in Alabama?
sections.html:
Either the district court or the circuit court, depending on their established jurisdictions, and the case belongs in the county where the rented property sits. Section 35-9A-461(b) of the Alabama Code says eviction actions get precedence in scheduling over all other civil cases.

The landlord's lawsuit follows the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure and the Alabama Rules of Appellate Procedure, except where the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act changes them. In plain terms, an Alabama eviction is a regular civil case that has been put on a faster track.

For an owner of a rented house, the county line matters. A house in Madison County is heard in Madison County, and a house in Mobile County is heard in Mobile County, even if the landlord lives somewhere else.

sections.h2: What are the steps of an Alabama eviction from notice to writ?
sections.html:
The usual path runs from a written termination notice, to a lawsuit, to a judgment, to a writ of possession. The statute does not give a single calendar for the whole thing, so the days below come only from the sections cited.

StepWhat the Code saysSection
Termination notice, unpaid rentLease ends if rent and late fees are not paid within seven business days after receipt35-9A-421(b)
Termination notice, other breachTermination date not less than seven business days after receipt, unless cured35-9A-421(a)
Lawsuit filedDistrict or circuit court in the property county, with scheduling precedence35-9A-461(b)
Appeal windowSeven days after entry of the district court eviction judgment35-9A-461(d)
Writ of possessionIssues on the landlord's application, after a seven day automatic stay35-9A-461(e)

The notice periods run in business days, so weekends and holidays stretch them.

sections.h2: How does a tenant get served with an eviction lawsuit in Alabama?
sections.html:
Service follows the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure, with a special fallback written into the landlord and tenant statute. If a sheriff, constable or process server cannot reach the defendant in person, Section 35-9A-461(c) allows two alternatives.

  • Delivering the notice to any person who is sui juris, meaning legally able to act, and lives on the premises.
  • If after reasonable effort no one is found living there, posting a copy on the door of the premises.
  • A mailing step follows the posting: on the day of posting or by the close of the next business day, the notice of filing must be sent by first class mail to the premises' mailing address, or to the defendant's last known address if the premises has none.
  • Service by posting is complete as of the date of mailing.

The statute also directs that an entry of the posting and mailing be made on the return filed in the case.

sections.h2: How long does a tenant have to appeal an Alabama eviction judgment?
sections.html:
Seven days after the entry of judgment. Any party can appeal an eviction judgment entered by a district court to the circuit court within that window, and the statute sets this deadline notwithstanding the general appeal rule in Section 12-12-70(a).

A timely post-judgment motion under the civil rules suspends the clock. The full appeal time then runs from the date the order on that motion is entered, or from the date the motion is denied by operation of law under Rule 59.1.

When either side appeals, the clerk schedules the case for trial as a preferred case and it is to be set within 60 days of the filing of the appeal.

sections.h2: Does a tenant's appeal stop the eviction in Alabama?
sections.html:
Only if the tenant pays rent into court. Section 35-9A-461(d) says a tenant's appeal to circuit court or to an appellate court does not prevent a writ of restitution or possession unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk all rent properly payable under the lease since the date the action was filed.

The tenant must then keep paying each rent installment to the clerk as it comes due while the appeal is pending. If there is a dispute about the amount, the court decides what is properly payable.

  • If the tenant misses a payment, the court on motion shall issue the writ and the landlord is placed in full possession.
  • When the appeal ends, the court tells the clerk what to do with the money paid in.
  • If the landlord took possession and the judgment is later reversed, the circuit court may issue a writ to restore the tenant, but not as against a third party.

sections.h2: What happens after the judge rules for the landlord?
sections.html:
A writ of possession issues when the landlord applies for it, and the statute adds a seven day automatic stay on that writ. Section 35-9A-461(e) says that seven day period applies notwithstanding Rule 62 of the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure.

If a tenant removed under the writ re-enters the home without just cause, the tenant can be held in contempt, and successive writs may issue as needed to carry out the judgment. The Code does not, in the section cited here, set out who carries out the removal or how many days the tenant gets to pack.

Anyone planning a sale around a tenant's departure should treat the seven day stay and a possible appeal as the first two moving parts, then ask the court clerk or an attorney what the local practice is for the writ.

sections.h2: What other Alabama rules can change how an eviction plays out?
sections.html:
Four sections of the landlord and tenant act tend to come up. Each one is short enough to summarize, and each can be checked on the legislature's or Justia's copy of the Code.

  • Holdover (35-9A-441(c)): a tenant who stays after the term or termination without consent can be sued for possession. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, the landlord may also recover up to three months' periodic rent or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus reasonable attorney fees.
  • Month-to-month notice (35-9A-441(b)): either side may end a month-to-month tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice.
  • Retaliation (35-9A-501): a landlord may not raise rent, cut services or bring an action for possession because the tenant complained to a code agency, complained about maintenance, or joined a tenants' group. The landlord can still sue for possession when the tenant is in default on rent, or for other material lease violations.
  • Security deposits (35-9A-201): money held as security may be applied to accrued rent and damages, with an itemized written notice and any balance delivered 60 days after the tenancy ends and possession is delivered.

Section 35-9A-201 also caps most deposits at one month's periodic rent, with exceptions for pets, changes to the premises and increased liability risks.

sections.h2: Can I sell a rented house in Alabama while an eviction is pending?
sections.html:
Owners do it, and the practical question is whether the buyer will take the house with the tenant or the court case still open. Some buyers want the home empty first. We can look at an as-is house with the process still under way.

Before agreeing to anything, an owner should know four facts: whether a termination notice has been delivered, whether a suit has been filed, whether a judgment has been entered, and whether any appeal money has been paid into the circuit court. Those four answers tell a buyer how much time and risk remain.

We buy houses as they stand, including rentals with tenant problems. Tell our team where your case is, and we can talk about timing without asking you to fix, clean or list the house first.

faqs.q: Which court hears an eviction case in Alabama?
faqs.a: The district court or the circuit court, based on their jurisdiction, in the county where the property is. Section 35-9A-461(b) gives eviction actions precedence over other civil cases in scheduling.

faqs.q: How many days does a tenant have to appeal an Alabama eviction?
faqs.a: Seven days after the district court enters the eviction judgment. A timely post-judgment motion suspends that period until the court rules on it.

faqs.q: Does an appeal keep the tenant in the house?
faqs.a: Not by itself. The appeal does not prevent a writ of possession unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk the rent due since the filing date and keeps paying rent as it comes due.

faqs.q: What is the automatic stay on a writ of possession?
faqs.a: After a judgment for the landlord and an application for the writ, Section 35-9A-461(e) sets the automatic stay at seven days, replacing the general stay in Rule 62.

faqs.q: How is a tenant served if the sheriff cannot find them?
faqs.a: The papers may be delivered to a person living on the premises, or posted on the door if no one is found, followed by first class mail the same day or by the close of the next business day.

faqs.q: How fast must an appealed eviction be tried?
faqs.a: The clerk schedules it as a preferred case and it is to be set for trial within 60 days of the filing of the appeal, according to Section 35-9A-461(d).
